sources.title: «Deutliche Botschaften»: Fanszenen erhöhen Druck im Streit um Regionalliga-Reform

en.title: German fan groups plan protests over regional league reform
en.dek: Fan groups are organizing stadium protests to support the 'compass model' reform ahead of the German Football Association's 18 December vote.
facts: The DFB-Bundestag will vote on the regional league reform on 18 December in Frankfurt.
The reform requires a two-thirds majority to pass because it involves a change to the DFB statutes.
The 'compass model' is the preferred reform plan of DFB President Bernd Neuendorf.
The Nordostdeutscher Fußballverband (NOFV) and the North German association have withdrawn their support for the model.
body: German fan groups announced plans for protests in stadiums this weekend to support the 'compass model' for regional league reform. The alliance of fan groups stated they intend to send messages to clubs and stadiums regarding the proposal.

The Nordostdeutscher Fußballverband (NOFV) and the North German association have shifted their positions and now oppose the model. NOFV President Hermann Winkler stated the change in direction was due to potential negative impacts on leagues below the regional level.

DFB President Bernd Neuendorf designated the reform as a matter for his office, though the required two-thirds majority for the 18 December vote is currently in question. The West German Football Association supports the model, while the South German and Southwest associations have opposed it since the beginning.

The fan alliance accused the presidents of the North, Bavaria, and Northeast associations of prioritizing their own influence over reform interests. Hansa Rostock and other clubs in the northeast have publicly distanced themselves from the actions taken by their regional associations.
en.context: The DFB is seeking to reorganize the regional leagues. Because this change affects the structure of the leagues, it must be approved by a two-thirds majority of the DFB-Bundestag.

problemsFixed: The draft contains a summary sentence at the end of the final paragraph ('Several clubs...').
The draft uses 'remains uncertain' which borders on speculation/prediction.
The draft uses 'declared the reform a priority' which is a slight paraphrase of 'Chefsache' (a German idiom for a matter for the boss); it should be more precise.
The draft includes a 'context' field that repeats information already in the body.
